characters: Mansa: a fourteen-year-old Ghanaian JHS 2 student holding a notebook and calculator, observant and methodical.
Tetteh: her thirteen-year-old cousin in the same compound house, keen on physics and electronics.
Uncle Nii: a frustrated compound-house tenant staring at a beeping prepaid electricity meter.
Master Owusu: an Energy Commission-certified electrician in insulated boots, carrying a multimeter.

narrationPlan.voice: Sharp, curious teen voices for Mansa and Tetteh; anxious tenant voice for Uncle Nii; calm, principled electrician voice for Master Owusu
narrationPlan.pace: Practical, investigative, and clear (about 125 words per minute)
notes: Read dialogue with distinct, natural voices for each JHS student, teacher, and community specialist.
Pause for two seconds at each comprehension check so learners can reason before answering.
Never rush the final page: let the scientific and moral synthesis settle clearly.

music: Crisp acoustic plucking with a steady rhythmic tick like a meter pulse, resolving warmly (placeholder)
culturalNotes: NaCCA CCP Alignment: Integrated Science (B8.4.2.1 / B9.4.2.1 & B8.4.3.1: Electricity and electronics—power P = VI, energy in kWh, fuses, earthing, circuit breakers, and energy conservation), Social Studies (B7.1.1.2 & B8.4.1.1: Civic responsibility, protecting public utilities, and energy conservation), and RME (B8.6.1.1 / B9.6.1.1: Strand 6: Religion and Economic Life—money, honesty, integrity, and anti-corruption).

BECE Physics Clarity: Distinguishes clearly between Power (rate in watts/kilowatts) and Energy (total consumption in kilowatt-hours = kW × h)—one of the most frequently tested and confused JHS calculations.
Safety Guardrail: Students only read manufacturer rating plates on unplugged appliances; all wiring inspection is performed by an Energy Commission-certified electrician.

Illustrative usage assumptions behind “nearly twice as long”: before, about 18.2 kWh/day; after, about 9.09 kWh/day. These are modelled values; actual savings depend on appliance cycling and usage habits.
reviewQuestions: Is the language right for the stated JHS age band (Basic 7 to Basic 9) and BECE conceptual level?
Is anything here scientifically inaccurate, stereotyped, or unsafe for adolescents?

teacherGuide.overview: Turns a familiar Ghanaian compound-house dispute over prepaid meter credit into a hands-on physics, civic citizenship, and moral integrity lesson.
learningGoals: Calculate electrical power (P = V × I) and domestic electrical energy in kilowatt-hours (E = P × t).
Explain how damaged fridge seals, heating elements, and overloaded sockets waste energy and cause fires.
Analyse the economic and infrastructure damage caused by illegal electricity connections.
Apply RME principles of honesty and trustworthiness to shared utility use.

beforeReading: Show an unplugged 9 W LED bulb box and an unplugged 1,500 W iron rating plate: roughly how many LED bulbs draw the same power as one iron? (About 167.)
whileReading: Pause on Page 2 to verify why 300 W running 24 hours (7.2 kWh/day) beats brief lighting use.
afterReading: Conduct a safe home rating-plate survey (unplugged appliances only) and rank top three energy users.
discussion: Why do heating and cooling appliances use far more kWh than radios or LEDs?
reflection: Which single energy-wasting habit can you help fix in your home or classroom today?

mathsExtension.task: A 300 W refrigerator with a torn seal runs its compressor continuously for 24 hours. How many kWh does it use in one day, and how much is saved daily if fixing the seal cuts compressor run-time to 10 hours?
mathsExtension.answer: Faulty: 0.3 kW × 24 h = 7.2 kWh/day. Repaired: 0.3 kW × 10 h = 3.0 kWh/day. Daily saving = 4.2 kWh.

mathsExtension.task: At Ghana’s 230 V domestic mains supply, what current (I) does a 2,070 W electric kettle draw? Which standard fuse rating (3 A, 5 A, or 13 A) is appropriate?
mathsExtension.answer: I = P ÷ V = 2,070 ÷ 230 = 9 A. Of the listed ratings, 13 A is the suitable plug-fuse choice for a compatible appliance and plug; the correct protection must also follow the manufacturer’s instructions and applicable electrical standards.

support: Provide a conversion triangle card: divide watts by 1,000 first to get kilowatts before multiplying by hours.
stretch: Research Energy Commission Ghana star-rating labels (1-star to 5-star) on refrigerators and air conditioners.

factCheck.claim: Electrical energy consumed equals power in kilowatts multiplied by time in hours (E = P × t).
factCheck.explanation: Meters measure kilowatt-hours (kWh). Overloaded thin extension cords overheat by Joule heating (I²R), causing insulation failure and fire risks.
factCheck.reference: NaCCA CCP Integrated Science B8.4.2.1 / B9.4.2.1 & Energy Commission Ghana domestic wiring guidelines.
